topicTitle: Nitrogen: reason for inertness of nitrogen and active nitrogen; chemical properties of ammonia and applications and harmful effects of ammonia
notes: **Inertness:** $N_2$ has a very strong triple bond (946 kJ/mol) and no dipole moment, making it chemically unreactive at ordinary conditions.
**Active nitrogen:** produced by passing an electric discharge through $N_2$. It is an allotrope containing atomic nitrogen and excited molecules, extremely reactive.
**Ammonia preparation:** Haber process: $N_2 + 3H_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3$, $\Delta H = -92.4\,\text{kJ}$. High pressure (200 atm), moderate temperature (450Â°C), iron catalyst with promoters.
**Ammonia properties:** pungent gas, highly soluble in water forming weak base $NH_4OH$. Reacts with acids to form ammonium salts, with $CuSO_4$ to give deep blue complex, with $Na$ to form sodamide.
**Applications:** fertilizers (urea, ammonium nitrate), refrigerants, cleaning agents, explosives. Harmful effects: toxic if inhaled, caustic burns, contributes to eutrophication in waterways.
